question: How do I generate a typed TypeScript or Rust client for a deployed contract or a local Wasm artifact with the Stellar CLI?

golden.answer: Use the language subcommand. `stellar contract bindings typescript --output-dir <dir>` takes one of `--wasm <file>`, `--wasm-hash <hash>`, or `--contract-id <C…>`, but the CLI marks it deprecated in favor of the JS SDK generator (`npx @stellar/stellar-sdk generate`). `stellar contract bindings rust` works only from a local `--wasm`, so for an on-chain contract first fetch its Wasm. Python, Java, Flutter, Swift, PHP, and Kotlin Multiplatform are placeholders that require an external plugin. Bindings snapshot the embedded spec, so regenerate after interface changes. `contractimport!` is the separate in-contract Rust typed-client macro.
keyFacts: TypeScript bindings take Wasm, hash, or contract ID but are deprecated for the JS SDK.
Rust bindings generate only from a local `--wasm` file.
Other languages are placeholders that need an external plugin.
Bindings snapshot the spec and must be regenerated after interface changes.
avoid: Do NOT claim that Rust or placeholder languages accept all three TypeScript inputs.
Do NOT claim that bindings update automatically after a contract upgrade.
golden.notes: Version-qualify CLI claims; the current CLI is 30.0.1 (2026-11-03).
